name: Pikali EU Withdrawal Button
author: pikali

sections.description:
Since 19 June 2026, every online shop selling to consumers in the European Union must let them withdraw from a contract online (Article 11a of Directive 2011/83/EU, inserted by Directive (EU) 2023/2673). A line in your terms or a PDF form is no longer enough: customers need a clearly labelled “Withdraw from contract here” function, a two-step declaration ending with a “Confirm withdrawal” button, and an immediate acknowledgement of receipt on a durable medium.

Pikali EU Withdrawal Button sets this up for WooCommerce in a minute, with nothing to paste.

What your customers get

  • A “Withdraw from contract here” link in the footer of every page, in My account, on their orders and in the order e-mails. The withdrawal page is created for you.
  • Guests find their order with its number and e-mail address; logged-in customers pick it from their orders.
  • A declaration step, then the mandatory “Confirm withdrawal” button. No reason required, optional comment.
  • A timestamped acknowledgement of receipt, on screen and by e-mail (a WooCommerce e-mail you can style like the others).
  • Keyboard and screen-reader friendly, mobile-ready, works without JavaScript.
  • The 24 official languages of the European Union, with the exact wording the directive imposes in each language for the two mandatory labels.

What you get

  • A copy of each declaration by e-mail, with the points to check flagged: late request, professional customer, excluded item, subscription, order not yet shipped.
  • A note on the order and a Withdrawals log (WooCommerce > Withdrawals): status, internal note, resend the acknowledgement, CSV export.
  • The deadline computed for you: 14 days from delivery (configurable), extended when it ends on a weekend or public holiday.
  • Late requests are recorded and flagged, never blocked: you decide. Nothing is refunded or cancelled automatically.
  • Proof you can rely on: server time, full content, IP address and SHA-256 fingerprint of each declaration; personal data anonymised automatically at the end of the retention period you choose.
  • Personal data notice (article 13 GDPR) under the forms, on by default, editable.
  • “Withdrawal form” block and shortcode; HPOS and cart/checkout blocks compatible.
  • Everything stays in your WordPress database: no account, no external service, no tracking.

Pro edition

The Pro edition adds withdrawal item by item (items and quantities), “Write to the customer” from the withdrawal record with 8 ready-made messages pre-filled in the customer’s language, and the EU harmonised notice on the legal guarantee of conformity (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1960) on product pages. It takes over the data and settings of the free edition. Discover the Pro edition.

Not legal advice

The plugin implements the online withdrawal function described by the directive. It does not replace your terms of sale, which must still describe the right of withdrawal and its conditions.
sections.installation:
1. Plugins > Add New, search for “Pikali EU Withdrawal Button”, install and activate (WooCommerce must be active).
  2. The withdrawal page is created and the link appears in the footer, in My account and in the order e-mails.
  3. Review WooCommerce > Settings > Withdrawal: return instructions, period, excluded products or categories, professional customers, retention period.
sections.faq:
Does it refund or cancel the order?

No. The plugin records the declaration, acknowledges it and informs you. Refunds, returns and cancellations stay in your hands, in WooCommerce.

What if a customer withdraws after the deadline?

The declaration is never blocked: it is recorded and flagged as late, and you decide.

Can a customer withdraw from only some items?

In the free edition the declaration covers the whole order, and the customer can list the items concerned in the comment. Withdrawal item by item is part of the Pro edition.

Which languages?

The 24 official languages of the European Union. The two labels whose wording is imposed by the directive (“Withdraw from contract here”, “Confirm withdrawal”) use the official text of each language version of the directive. The form follows the language of the site (WPML and Polylang supported).

Where is the data stored?

In a table of your own WordPress database. Nothing is sent to Pikali or to any third party.
sections.changelog:
1.5.4 — 2026-11-26

  • Translation-ready originals: every translatable string is now in English (plugin name instead of the French brand in notices, English block keyword), as requested by translate.wordpress.org.

1.5.3 — 2026-11-25

  • Review update: whole-order workflow packaged separately, footer output sanitization and explicit product-save checks.

1.5.2 — 2026-11-24

  • First release on WordPress.org: online withdrawal function, two-step declaration, acknowledgement of receipt, merchant copy, proof log, 24 EU languages.
